items.panel_name: HBsAg, HBeAg, HBV DNA and HCV RNA

review.note: NCT01797120: the footnote 'Patients on antiviral prophylaxis treatment or positive HBV antibodies should be tested for HBV-DNA ...' fires RT-1 (IS) on the annotation only; the row becomes weak and the HBDNA (MB) test-identity hit is set aside. The footnote says who is tested, not what is measured. Question for the rules: how an annotation-only rule match ranks against a label test-identity hit.
The protocols differ: NCT03548935 context lists four analytes (panel); NCT03693430 lists one, hsCRP (named test, no test code on the label).
The protocols differ: NCT03637764 names two analytes, isatuximab and atezolizumab (panel); NCT04557384 one, ramucirumab (named test, PC by RT-9).
The standalone row of the hbv dna queue entry: weak because of the annotation-only RT-1 match; the member HBV-DNA in the same study routes MB.
The only member from protocol context is the panel label itself, 'Urine drug screen (including cotinine)', routed LB via DRUGSCR (peeled hit). A panel that is its own member.

flags.note: Panel or named test. The targeted decisions run changed unsure to named test (finding kind pc), routed PC by RT-9. The lab_and_purpose entry also names pirtobrutinib in the same samples; the agent kept named test because the label names only rosuvastatin. A strict reading of the sample-collection rule would give panel.

review.note: Stays open. Named test gives PC; panel (rosuvastatin and pirtobrutinib in the same samples) would give 'panel, not split' and lose the PC route. The label names only rosuvastatin.

flags.note: Other or panel. The footnote lists survival, subsequent therapies and new malignancy.
